item.text: {"chapter_id":"8B","shard_id":"8B-S01","reviewed_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E002","BATCH-0002-E003","BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E007","BATCH-0002-E008","BATCH-0002-E010","BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0002-E012","BATCH-0002-E013","BATCH-0003-E001","BATCH-0003-E005","BATCH-0003-E006","BATCH-0003-E007","BATCH-0003-E008","BATCH-0003-E011","BATCH-0003-E012","BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0003-E019","BATCH-0003-E020","BATCH-0003-E021","BATCH-0003-E022","BATCH-0004-E001","BATCH-0004-E002","BATCH-0004-E003","BATCH-0004-E004","BATCH-0004-E006","BATCH-0004-E007","BATCH-0004-E008","BATCH-0004-E009","BATCH-0004-E010","BATCH-0004-E012","BATCH-0004-E013","BATCH-0004-E014","BATCH-0004-E015","BATCH-0004-E016","BATCH-0004-E017","BATCH-0005-E001","BATCH-0005-E002","BATCH-0005-E004","BATCH-0005-E006","BATCH-0005-E007","BATCH-0005-E008","BATCH-0005-E009","BATCH-0005-E010","BATCH-0006-E001","BATCH-0006-E003","BATCH-0006-E005","BATCH-0006-E006","BATCH-0007-E004","BATCH-0008-E002","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0008-E006","BATCH-0008-E008","BATCH-0008-E010","BATCH-0009-E001","BATCH-0009-E003","BATCH-0009-E004","BATCH-0009-E006","BATCH-0009-E007","BATCH-0009-E010","BATCH-0009-E011","BATCH-0010-E002","BATCH-0010-E005","BATCH-0010-E008","BATCH-0010-E009","BATCH-0010-E010","BATCH-0011-E001","BATCH-0011-E002","BATCH-0011-E003","BATCH-0011-E005","BATCH-0011-E006","BATCH-0011-E007","BATCH-0011-E008"],"answers":[{"question_id":"8B.1","answer":"The shard provides evidence of a partly explicit and partly revealed program: López Obrador was presented as pursuing a break with neoliberal policy, corruption, violence, and deference to U.S. interests; later evidence shows explicit priorities of energy self-sufficiency through fossil fuels, expanded military-led security and state projects, large infrastructure projects, and a promised Ayotzinapa investigation. However, some program evidence is publisher or retrospective description rather than a formal presidential text, and official claims are contested.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E001","BATCH-0004-E016","BATCH-0004-E017","BATCH-0003-E008","BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0007-E004","BATCH-0010-E009","BATCH-0011-E003","BATCH-0011-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0006-E001","BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0008-E003"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not provide a complete dated manifesto or consolidated program portfolio.","Some goals are inferred from repeated policy choices and public defenses, so attribution and goal breadth remain incomplete."]},{"question_id":"8B.2","answer":"The shard shows extensive translation of selected priorities into legislation, budgets, institutional arrangements, appointments, directives, and projects. Examples include military control of the National Guard and expanded armed-forces responsibilities, infrastructure and energy projects, a National Search Commission and human-identification initiatives, nuclear-safety institutions, and planned or approved social and health measures. Translation was uneven: judicially invalidated military-control arrangements, incomplete environmental authorizations, unresolved transparency reforms, and disputed appointments show institutional and legal limits.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E006","BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0004-E001","BATCH-0004-E002","BATCH-0004-E003","BATCH-0004-E010","BATCH-0005-E001","BATCH-0005-E009","BATCH-0006-E001","BATCH-0007-E004","BATCH-0010-E005","BATCH-0010-E008","BATCH-0010-E010","BATCH-0011-E003","BATCH-0011-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0004-E009","BATCH-0006-E005","BATCH-0009-E001","BATCH-0009-E004","BATCH-0010-E008"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Several budget and legislative items concern proposals or institutional actors rather than personally directed presidential decisions.","The shard does not establish complete execution of every enacted measure."]},{"question_id":"8B.3","answer":"The shard documents substantial mobilization of the state and ruling network toward military-led security, infrastructure, social programs, migration enforcement, and nuclear safety. It includes large deployments, military construction and operations, federal budgets and agencies, and documented evaluation or safety resources. It also records major control failures, financial irregularities, transparency gaps, and weak accountability, indicating mobilization that was broad but uneven and sometimes poorly controlled.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E007","BATCH-0002-E008","BATCH-0003-E006","BATCH-0003-E011","BATCH-0004-E001","BATCH-0004-E002","BATCH-0005-E002","BATCH-0007-E004","BATCH-0008-E008","BATCH-0010-E002","BATCH-0011-E001","BATCH-0011-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E005","BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0004-E012","BATCH-0004-E015","BATCH-0005-E004","BATCH-0010-E010","BATCH-0011-E001"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Administrative mobilization is better documented than its effectiveness across the full program portfolio.","Nuclear evidence is primarily attributed to CFE and CNSNS, not personally to López Obrador."]},{"question_id":"8B.4","answer":"The shard shows deliberate use of capable or loyal implementers in some domains: trained nuclear personnel, succession planning, CFE’s Nuclear Corporate Coordination, military leadership, and selected search-commission appointments. It also records concerns about inexperienced appointments, replacement of the National Search Commission head after a disputed recount, and alleged favoritism or nepotism involving associates and family networks. Attribution of individual personnel choices is mixed.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E008","BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0004-E003","BATCH-0005-E001","BATCH-0005-E004","BATCH-0010-E009","BATCH-0011-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0004-E008","BATCH-0005-E004","BATCH-0008-E008","BATCH-0011-E001"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not provide systematic performance records for most presidential appointees.","Several nepotism and conflict-of-interest claims are allegations or retrospective investigative reporting rather than final findings."]},{"question_id":"8B.5","answer":"Coordination and reach were substantial in selected projects: military and civilian agencies coordinated infrastructure, emergency response, migration, and nuclear-safety programs; the military operated across national territory and government functions. Conversely, evidence shows incomplete coordination, weak civil oversight, missing detention records, transparency failures, institutional resistance, incomplete project access, and unresolved Ayotzinapa cooperation. The record therefore shows broad reach but inconsistent compliance and coordination quality.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E007","BATCH-0002-E010","BATCH-0003-E006","BATCH-0003-E011","BATCH-0003-E012","BATCH-0003-E022","BATCH-0004-E001","BATCH-0005-E002","BATCH-0008-E002","BATCH-0008-E008","BATCH-0009-E003","BATCH-0010-E002","BATCH-0010-E009","BATCH-0011-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0004-E009","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0009-E010","BATCH-0011-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard provides no comprehensive ministry-by-ministry or regional compliance dataset.","Some reported coordination failures may reflect subordinate institutional resistance rather than direct presidential incapacity."]},{"question_id":"8B.6","answer":"The shard contains abundant observable implementation: military deployments and assigned tasks, infrastructure construction and openings, social and health measures, nuclear authorizations and safety systems, emergency procedures, and search-commission platforms. It also records incomplete or symbolic implementation, including projects opened unfinished, delayed or missing environmental approvals, persistent disappearance-investigation failures, unregistered detentions, weak protection mechanisms, financial irregularities, and unresolved military accountability.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0002-E012","BATCH-0002-E013","BATCH-0003-E005","BATCH-0003-E006","BATCH-0003-E007","BATCH-0003-E012","BATCH-0004-E001","BATCH-0004-E002","BATCH-0004-E003","BATCH-0004-E006","BATCH-0004-E010","BATCH-0005-E002","BATCH-0005-E006","BATCH-0005-E009","BATCH-0006-E003","BATCH-0007-E004","BATCH-0008-E010","BATCH-0009-E003","BATCH-0010-E002","BATCH-0010-E008","BATCH-0010-E009","BATCH-0011-E001","BATCH-0011-E002","BATCH-0011-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E005","BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0004-E009","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0009-E006","BATCH-0011-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Implementation evidence is concentrated in security, infrastructure, nuclear safety, and selected social programs.","The shard does not establish final service quality or durable operation for many newly opened projects."]},{"question_id":"8B.7","answer":"Progress toward selected goals was mixed. Favorable evidence includes reported poverty reduction, increased minimum wages and redistributive spending, nuclear-safety implementation, some search and identification activity, and construction or opening of flagship projects. Adverse or contrary evidence includes persistent violence and disappearances, unresolved Ayotzinapa, weak justice and protection outcomes, fossil-fuel policy judged critically insufficient for climate goals, incomplete and costly infrastructure, and outcomes confounded by external actors, inherited conditions, and disputed attribution.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E013","BATCH-0003-E005","BATCH-0003-E007","BATCH-0003-E008","BATCH-0003-E011","BATCH-0003-E012","BATCH-0004-E003","BATCH-0004-E012","BATCH-0005-E002","BATCH-0006-E003","BATCH-0007-E004","BATCH-0010-E009","BATCH-0011-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E005","BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0004-E004","BATCH-0006-E006","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0009-E010","BATCH-0011-E001","BATCH-0011-E002"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Several outcome indicators end in 2022 or are administration-wide rather than directly presidential.","The shard lacks a complete baseline-to-end-period counterfactual assessment across all stated goals."]},{"question_id":"8B.8","answer":"There is strong evidence of adaptation in nuclear safety and emergency management: audits, self-assessments, corrective-action programs, drills, revised procedures, training changes, and design modifications produced documented follow-up. There is also evidence of adaptation in some economic and infrastructure decisions. However, other evidence shows rigid or counterproductive responses: continuation of disputed military arrangements, failure to compel military cooperation in Ayotzinapa, disputed recount and replacement decisions in the disappearance registry, incomplete correction of cybersecurity and transparency failures, and projects repeatedly redesigned under legal or political pressure.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E002","BATCH-0002-E003","BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E007","BATCH-0002-E010","BATCH-0002-E012","BATCH-0004-E016","BATCH-0006-E003","BATCH-0008-E006","BATCH-0010-E008","BATCH-0011-E003","BATCH-0011-E007"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0004-E008","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0009-E010","BATCH-0011-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most adaptive evidence concerns implementing agencies rather than presidential learning.","The shard does not consistently show whether corrective actions were completed or effective."]},{"question_id":"8B.9","answer":"The ruler and government made formal and operational crisis responses involving military deployment, migration enforcement, Hurricane Otis relief, emergency preparedness, nuclear safety, and institutional resistance. Some responses maintained operational continuity and delivered emergency or infrastructure capacity. Other responses prioritized military control despite a constitutional ruling, defended institutions against documented criticism, failed to secure Ayotzinapa cooperation, and used confrontational rhetoric toward courts, journalists, activists, and critics. Allegations and institutional findings must not be treated as proof of personal intent in every case.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E010","BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0003-E006","BATCH-0003-E012","BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0003-E022","BATCH-0004-E004","BATCH-0004-E006","BATCH-0004-E009","BATCH-0005-E001","BATCH-0005-E009","BATCH-0007-E004","BATCH-0008-E002","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0009-E001","BATCH-0009-E004","BATCH-0010-E002","BATCH-0011-E003","BATCH-0011-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0004-E012","BATCH-0004-E013","BATCH-0004-E014","BATCH-0009-E007","BATCH-0010-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard offers no full assessment of longer-term Hurricane Otis recovery or international crisis outcomes.","Some crisis conduct is reported by advocacy or journalistic sources and remains contested."]},{"question_id":"8B.10","answer":"By the end of 2023, the shard shows durable or potentially durable institutional and physical changes in military deployment, infrastructure, energy, social administration, nuclear safety, and some legal protections. It also shows fragility and incomplete conversion: flagship works opened unfinished, costs exceeded initial estimates, one train phase stopped shortly after opening, environmental and legal disputes persisted, military control was judicially invalidated, transparency weakened, and major disappearance and security objectives remained unresolved. End-period durability and achieved outcomes therefore remain mixed and partly unverified.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0002-E004","BATCH-0002-E013","BATCH-0003-E008","BATCH-0003-E015","BATCH-0004-E001","BATCH-0004-E002","BATCH-0005-E008","BATCH-0007-E004","BATCH-0008-E008","BATCH-0009-E006","BATCH-0010-E005","BATCH-0010-E009","BATCH-0011-E002","BATCH-0011-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E005","BATCH-0003-E016","BATCH-0004-E008","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0009-E001","BATCH-0009-E010","BATCH-0011-E001","BATCH-0011-E007"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The shard does not provide post-2023 evidence sufficient to establish long-term durability.","Several flagship projects were newly opened, so achieved outcomes, financial sustainability, and institutional persistence were not yet observable."]}],"cross_shard_cautions":["The evidence is heavily concentrated on security, militarization, infrastructure, nuclear safety, transparency, disappearances, and selected welfare measures; it does not cover the complete national program portfolio.","Nuclear-safety evidence is generally attributed to CFE, CNSNS, SENER, and federal government institutions rather than personally to López Obrador.","Official claims, allegations, advocacy findings, journalistic reports, and judicial findings are distinct evidentiary types and should not be collapsed.","The shard contains substantial inherited-baseline, subordinate-action, external-shock, legal-constraint, and causal-attribution uncertainty; no score is assigned here."]}
